To file a legal action against someone, generally a non-criminal (civil) action.

examples.text: sue someone for selling a faulty product
I plan to sue you for everything you have.
He was sued by the late Geo. Walpole Leake for slander, and after two trials, occupying eight days, he was mulcted in heavy damages and costs.

glosses: To seek by request; to make application; to petition; to entreat; to plead.

examples.text: The king of Bimsa sued for peace after Nynal's armies overran his territory; he knew any further resistance would only harm the common people.

To follow.

examples.text: And the olde knyght seyde unto the yonge knyght, ‘Sir, swith me.’
examples.translation: And the old knight said to the young knight, 'Sir, follow me'.
examples.english: And the old knight said to the young knight, 'Sir, follow me'.

To inform on, to rat out; to tell a person in authority that someone else has done something wrong.

examples.text: My sister told on me when I didn't go to school.
Lest they should tell on us, saying, So did David.

glosses: To cause visible strain to.

examples.text: Years of drinking started to tell on his body.

glosses: wyrażać słownie swoje skargi

examples.text: – Prawdziwe piekło! O mało nie zostałam stratowana – skarżyła się pani Barbara, emerytka z Mokotowa.

glosses: To express feelings of pain, dissatisfaction, or resentment.

examples.text: Joe was always complaining about the noise made by his neighbours.
O loſs of ſight, of thee I moſt complain!

glosses: To make a formal accusation or bring a formal charge.

examples.text: They've complained about me to the police again.
Now, Master Shallow, you'll complain of me to the king?
If you get cheated by the Better Business Bureau, who do you complain to?

glosses: To creak or squeak, as a timber or wheel.

examples.text: the complaining bed-springs

glosses: A low thundering, rumbling or growling sound.
The sound made by a hungry stomach.
A surly complaint.

examples.text: That whiner is never without a grumble to share.

glosses: To make a low, growling or rumbling noise, like a hungry stomach or certain animals.

examples.text: The distant thunder grumbles.
It made his stomach grumble in protest to think the mule was eating, and here he was worrying about her with an empty belly of his own.

glosses: To complain; to murmur or mutter with discontent; to make ill-natured complaints in a low voice and a surly manner.

examples.text: He grumbles about the food constantly, but has yet to learn to cook.

glosses: To utter in a grumbling fashion.

examples.text: He grumbled that there was no grain "in the country" and that people were talking instead of working to provide it.

glosses: Accuser, dénoncer.
